Sheet1: PubChem Substance IDentifier, a unique identifier for chemical substances assigned by the PubChem database
Primary Mode of Action, the main mechanism by which the sample exerts its effects in cellular systems
Name or description of the assay sample was tested in
Library or collection containing the sample
Chemical Abstracts Service registry number, a unique numerical identifier assigned to chemical substances
Alternative name or identifier for the sample
Half-maximal effective concentration (EC50 or IC50) of the sample, a measure of potency
Logarithm of the AC50 from a fit of the data to the Hill equation (calculated based on Molar Units)
Area Under the Curve, a measure of the overall response of the sample in the assay. Calculated as the integral of the dose-response curve of compound activity across all measured dose points.

Classification of sample dose-response curves, based on the quality of curve fit to the data (r2), the magnitude of the response (efficacy), and the number of asymptotes to the calculated curve. See https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.0604348103 for more information.
Official drug name of sample, if applicable
Maximal efficacy of sample, reported as a percentage of control. These values are estimated based on fits of the Hill equation to the dose-response curves
Maximum activity observed for sample (generally at highest concentration tested)
p-value calculated from curve fitting, indicating statistical significance of the fit
Coefficient of determination, a measure of the goodness of fit of a curve. Closer to 1.0 equates to better Hill equation fit
Gene ID number for the gene associated with the sample, where applicable (assigned by National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI))
Symbol for the gene associated with the sample, where applicable (assigned by the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (HGNC))
Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System notation, a compact representation of the chemical structure
Name of the supplier or source of the sample

Experimental activity of sample at a given dose point. Values represent % normalized response, and are scaled to experimental positive and negative control responses. Numerical suffixes range from 0 to 14, and indicate which sample dose point [conc0 - conc14] corresponds to which data point. E.g. data0 was the % normalized response measured in the asasy at sample concentration conc0.

Final in-well concentration of sample (Molar, in Scientific exponential format) at each experimental dose point. Numerical suffixes range from 0 to 14, and indicate which data point [data0 - data14] corresponds to which dose point.
